newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St George says improvement challenging.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St George says improvement challenging.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Tuesday that it would be a challenge to improve its results in the first half of the 1996/97 year, given possible distractions linked to its merger with Advance Bank Ltd and strong pressure on margins.
"The challenge is undoubtedly there," St George Bank managing director Jim Sweeney told a news conference, when asked whether St George could improve its first half profit.
Sweeney repeated comments made with St George's annual results released earlier, that results for the year to September 30, 1997 were likely to be flatter than in 1995/96.
St George reported a net profit after accounting for preference dividends of A$148.3 million for the 1995/96 year, a rise of 9.4 percent.
Profits after accounting for prefs and before abnormals rose 9.9 percent to A$155.1 million, up slightly on the A$152 million median analyst forecast.
Sweeney said he saw home lending margins falling to 100 to 150 basis points across the industry.

Currently retail home lending margins are between 200 and 250 basis points for the major banks, but Sweeney said some of St George's products were already operating on margins of 150 basis points or less.
He said banks in Australia had traditionally enjoyed margins of 350 to 450 basis points before the entrance of non-bank competitors funded from mortage origination.
"I think we'll be looking much nearer to 150 basis points or even 100 basis points," he said of industry margins.
He said St George would work to protect the group margin by continuing to diversify into non-residential lending and by controlling operating and borrowing costs.
St George was also already budgeting for a doubling of fee income from retail banking products because of fee increases introduced late in 1995/96.

Sweeney pointed to St George's group interest margin as at September 30, 1996, which was 352 basis points, an increase over the 347 points a year earlier as proof of St George's ability to preserve group margins.
He said however he was reluctant to predict that St George would again be able to again increase the group's margin in 1996/97.
He also said banks were also under pressure to reduce bank fees to secure market share.
"The market is so competitive at the moment that I'd like to be able to say to you that, yes, that banks will pick up the lost margin from revenue on fees," he said.
"But the competition is so tough that almost all banks are trading away fees and charges to gain the assets on their books," he said.
Sweeney said St George was also determined not lose market share.
"We are determined not to surrender our market to anybody, be they major banks or non-bank originators, so that means we have to stand in the market and compete," he said.
"Enough has already been said to indicate there will be further margin pressure there," he said
"We expect that the result could be flatter and we may not be able to enjoy the margins that we have, but in relative terms to our competitors, I'm very confident of our ability there."
-- Bernard Hickey -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1812
